title: Mindfulness of Allah gives you a way to tell right from wrong.
subtitle: Clarity as a gift of taqwa

row.title: a criterion
sub: truth from falsehood, a way out

then: Early scholars explained the Furqan here as {reward}a way out, salvation, help,{/reward} and Ibn Ishaq as a criterion between truth and falsehood. Ibn Kathir says the last includes the others: {idea}those who keep their duty to Allah are guided to tell the true from the false,{/idea} and given a way out of their affairs.
now: You are stuck on a decision: the job offer, the marriage proposal, the business partner. Pros and cons lists, endless advice. {idea}The verse points somewhere else.{/idea} Clean up what is between you and Allah, and the right path often becomes easier to see.
old: If I think hard enough, I'll know what's right.
new: Guarding my conduct with Allah clears my sight. Clarity is His gift.
try: Facing a decision? Drop one thing you know displeases Allah this week, and pray istikhara.

title: They planned, and Allah planned. He is the best of planners.
subtitle: The night of the plot in Makkah
then: The chiefs of Quraysh met to decide what to do with the Prophet ﷺ: imprison him, expel him, or kill him. {trap}They settled on killing him with young men from every tribe.{/trap} Jibril told the Prophet ﷺ not to sleep in his bed that night, and {idea}Allah gave him permission to migrate.{/idea}
now: Someone is working against you at work. The family has already decided about you without asking. The odds in the meeting room look stacked. {idea}They plan, and Allah plans.{/idea} Do your part honestly and leave the outcome with the best of planners.
old: When people with power gang up against me, I'm finished.
new: Their plans sit inside Allah's plan. He is the best of planners.
try: If someone is working against you, make dua for Allah to handle it, and resist plotting back.

title: We could say something like this, they boasted.
subtitle: Big talk to avoid being moved
then: When the verses were recited, some in Quraysh said {trap}we have heard, we could say the like of this, it is just tales of the ancients.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes they boasted with words, not actions. {idea}They were challenged to bring even one chapter like it, and could not.{/idea}
now: Someone shares a moving reminder and your reflex is: I've heard this before, it's the same old stuff. Dismissing is easier than being touched. {idea}Calling something old is a quick way to avoid letting it in.{/idea}
old: I've heard all this before. It's nothing new.
new: Heard before does not mean taken in. Familiar words can still change me.
try: Take a verse you know well and read its meaning slowly, as if hearing it for the first time.

title: If this is true, then punish us, they said.
subtitle: The prayer they should have made instead
then: Anas said it was Abu Jahl who prayed: {trap}O Allah, if this is the truth from You, rain stones on us.{/trap} Ibn Kathir comments on the stubbornness of it. He points out what they should have said: {idea}O Allah, if this is the truth from You, guide us to it and help us follow it.{/idea}
now: Somewhere you may be daring the truth too. If quitting this really matters, life will show me. If praying is that important, something will happen. {idea}Swap the dare for a request.{/idea} If it is true, Allah, help me follow it.
old: If this really matters, I'll wait for a sign.
new: If something might be true, the honest prayer is: guide me to it.
try: Make the dua Ibn Kathir suggests: O Allah, if this is the truth, guide me to it and help me follow it.

title: Two shelters: the Prophet ﷺ among them, and seeking forgiveness.
subtitle: One shelter remains open for us
then: Ibn Abbas said {reward}they had two shelters: the Prophet ﷺ, and their seeking forgiveness.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said Allah sent down two safeguards for his community, and when he passed, {idea}seeking forgiveness would remain with them until the Day of Resurrection.{/idea}
now: Shaytan, the hadith says, vowed to keep misleading people as long as they live. Allah answered that He would keep forgiving as long as they ask. {idea}That shelter is open on the bus, at your desk, lying awake at night.{/idea}
old: I've messed up too much for asking forgiveness to matter.
new: As long as I keep asking, He keeps forgiving. That shelter is always open.
try: Say astaghfirullah slowly ten times today, thinking of one specific thing each time.

title: Only the mindful are true guardians of the House.
subtitle: Holding a sacred place is not the same as deserving it
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Quraysh deserved punishment, yet it was held back while the Prophet ﷺ was among them. They were {trap}keeping the believers from praying at the Sacred Mosque{/trap} while claiming to be its keepers. The verse says {idea}its true guardians are only those who are mindful of Allah.{/idea}
now: You may hold a role at the mosque, a seat on a committee, a title in the family. The position is not the point. {idea}How you treat people who come to pray, learn, or ask for help is.{/idea} Never be the reason someone feels unwelcome near Allah's house.
old: My role or position makes me a guardian of this place.
new: Only taqwa makes someone a true guardian. A title doesn't.
try: Next time you are at a mosque, welcome someone you don't know, especially someone new.

title: Their prayer at the House was whistling and clapping.
subtitle: Worship emptied of meaning
then: Ibn Abbas and many others said the Arabic words mean {trap}whistling and clapping.{/trap} Ibn Abbas described Quraysh going around the Kaaba whistling and clapping their hands. {idea}They stood at the holiest place and emptied the act of meaning.{/idea}
now: Your own prayer can thin out too: rushed, mind on the grocery list, finished before you noticed you started. {idea}Not a reason to give up, a reason to slow down.{/idea} Being in the right place is the start, not the whole of it.
old: I'm at the prayer, so I'm praying.
new: Prayer is presence, not just being there. I can bring my heart back.
try: In your next prayer, pause one breath after each movement and remember who you are standing before.

title: Money spent against the truth turns into regret.
subtitle: They will spend it, then grieve it
then: After Badr, men of Quraysh who had lost family asked those with wealth in the caravan to {trap}fund another fight against the Prophet ﷺ.{/trap} They agreed. Ibn Kathir says the verse is general: {trap}wealth spent to block the path of truth becomes anguish{/trap} and brings nothing in the end.
now: Think about where your own money quietly flows: the subscription you're ashamed of, the gift meant to win someone over against another, the bets you hide. {idea}Ask of every spend: will I be glad of this later?{/idea}
old: It's my money. Where it goes doesn't say much about me.
new: Where my money goes shows what I'm working for, and some spending ends in regret.
try: Look at last month's spending. Cancel or redirect one thing you would not want to answer for.

title: So Allah may separate the bad from the good.
subtitle: Trials sort what is hidden
then: Ibn Abbas explained the sorting as {idea}showing the difference between the people of happiness and the people of misery.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to 3:179: Allah would not leave the believers as they were {idea}until He distinguished the bad from the good.{/idea} The trials of that time drew out what was in each person.
now: A crisis at work shows who covers for whom. A family illness shows who shows up. {idea}Hard times also show you to yourself.{/idea} When pressure comes, ask what it is drawing out of you.
old: Hard times are just bad luck.
new: Hard times show what is inside me. I can choose what comes out.
try: Recall your last hard week. Name one good and one bad trait it revealed in you.

title: Stop now, and the past is forgiven.
subtitle: The door that stays open even for enemies
then: Even toward those who had fought him, the Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {reward}if they stop, their past will be forgiven.{/reward} He ﷺ said, {idea}Islam erases what came before it, and repentance erases what came before it.{/idea} The warning was for those who return to the same way.
now: You carry a past you're ashamed of: the years you drank, the things you said to your parents, the money you took. You think the door shut long ago. {reward}It hasn't.{/reward} The offer in this verse was made even to people who fought the Prophet ﷺ.
old: What I did is too much to ever be wiped away.
new: If even open enemies were offered a clean slate, the offer reaches me too.
try: Tonight, sincerely repent from one past sin you still carry, and resolve not to return to it.

title: Until no one is persecuted for their faith.
subtitle: What the struggle was for, and what it was not

row.title: courage, pride, show
sub: fighting for my people or image

then: Ibn Umar was pressed to cite this verse to join a fight among Muslims. He refused, explaining it was about {trap}the time when a believer was tortured or imprisoned for his faith.{/trap} He said that is nothing like {trap}fighting to gain leadership.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said the one in Allah's cause is {idea}the one who strives so that Allah's word is highest.{/idea}
now: Your struggles are smaller: the argument at the family dinner, the online debate, the battle for a promotion. {idea}Ask what is driving you.{/idea} Pride, your side winning, looking strong? Or something you would be glad to show Allah?
old: If my cause is right, my motives don't matter.
new: The cause is not enough. Why I strive is what Allah looks at.
try: Before your next disagreement, pause and ask yourself honestly why you want to win it.

title: Allah is your protector. What an excellent helper.
subtitle: When others turn away

row.title: their approval
sub: I need them on my side

then: After offering forgiveness to those who stop, the passage closes on those who turn away anyway. The believers, still few and surrounded, are told: {reward}know that Allah is your protector, an excellent protector and an excellent helper.{/reward} {idea}Their safety did not depend on the others' choice.{/idea}
now: You made the honest effort: the apology, the invitation, the olive branch. They turned away. You feel exposed and alone. {reward}You are not without a protector.{/reward} Their answer does not decide your standing with Allah.
old: If they reject me, I'm left with nothing.
new: Whoever turns away, Allah remains my protector and helper.
try: Think of one relationship where you did your part and were refused. Hand it to Allah in dua today.
